CO1: Trace a payment's inputs, outputs, change and implied fee
CO2: Explain how a transaction travels from wallet to network to block
CO3: Compute, as the whitepaper does, how confirmations reduce the chance of reversal
CO4: Describe a transaction chain as a provenance graph in W3C PROV terms
_note: These chapter objectives serve the course outcomes LO-2, LO-6, LO-7 and LO-1. LO-2, to trace one payment from a wallet to a confirmed block and say what each step guarantees, is the outcome this chapter carries almost on its own: the chapter follows a single real payment through construction, signing, propagation, the mempool, the fee, mining and confirmation, which is the outcome's own list of steps. Tracing a payment's inputs, outputs, change and implied fee also serves LO-6, which asks the student to read and construct transactions and to explain how a node decides that one is valid; the chapter supplies the reading half and names the signature and the script that a later chapter opens. Computing, as the whitepaper does, how confirmations reduce the chance of reversal serves LO-7, on how the network, the chain and proof of work together keep one ledger consistent, because the probability the whitepaper tabulates is exactly the quantitative form of what the chain of blocks defends against. The chapter's provenance and semantic-web objective is counted against LO-1, which asks the student to explain Bitcoin as a system and the parts it is built from, since describing a transaction chain in W3C PROV terms is a way of stating that structure exactly; this is the weakest of the four alignments, and the owner may prefer an outcome of its own for the course's semantic-web thread, which no draft outcome names. The ten course outcomes these objectives are aligned to are a DRAFT awaiting the owner's approval: 01-outcomes/sen0401_outcomes_v1_0_0.ttl states, in its own provenance header and in its rdfs:comment, that the outcomes are not approved and that the owner is asked to confirm, revise or reject each one. The alignment below is therefore provisional in the same way, and will be re-stated once the outcomes are ruled on.
